request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.
gaps: What specific types of engagement records are included in the 'full history'?
How will the system ensure that unauthorized users cannot access sensitive engagement records?
What happens to access rights for project managers if they leave or change roles?
How will data completeness and accuracy be verified beyond the assumption stated?
What measures are in place to handle confidential or diplomatic sensitivity in engagement records?

proposals.summary: This release allows project managers to view the full engagement history with a country before starting a new mission. It focuses on providing detailed engagement records to enhance decision-making and ensure better preparation for missions.

core_commitments.text: Enable project managers to view engagement history with countries.
Present comprehensive context for project managers to facilitate better mission planning.

in_scope.text: Project managers can access a dedicated engagement history section within the CRM for each country.
Engagement history will include records of past missions, meetings, and correspondence with each country.
Engagement records will display dates, participants, and summary notes of previous engagements.
Access to engagement history is restricted to project managers and regional coordinators.
The engagement history will be available in a user-friendly format that allows filtering by date and type of engagement.

out_of_scope.text: This release does not include features for automated engagement summaries or recommendations.
It will not integrate with external tools for engagement tracking beyond the CRM.
There will be no changes to user roles or permissions beyond specifying access for project managers and regional coordinators.

assumptions.text: Users accessing the engagement history are familiar with the CRM interface and functions.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request implies that project managers will be using the CRM to view engagement histories.

assumptions.text: The data regarding past engagements is complete and up-to-date in the CRM.
assumptions.why_implicit: The feature relies on the availability of accurate and comprehensive engagement data.

assumptions.text: Sensitive data within the engagement history has appropriate access control measures in place.
assumptions.why_implicit: Given the sensitivity of the data, proper security measures must exist for access.

definitions.definition: A detailed log that includes all recorded interactions, meetings, emails, and mission details related to a specified country.
A record that lists dates, participants, and summary notes for any interaction related to the country.

success_criteria.metric: Number of project managers who access the engagement history feature
success_criteria.target: At least 75% of project managers should access the feature within the first month of release.

C1.challenge: Access to engagement history is restricted to project managers and regional coordinators, but doesn't specify what happens to records that contain highly sensitive or diplomatic information. This lack of clarity can lead to unauthorized exposure of sensitive data.
C1.failure_scenario: A project manager accesses engagement history for a country that contains confidential diplomatic exchanges and shares this information with others who do not have the clearance to view it, resulting in a diplomatic breach.
C1.resolution_test: What specific data protection measures are in place to ensure that sensitive engagement records remain confidential?

history.text: Access to engagement history is restricted to project managers and regional coordinators, but doesn't specify what happens to records that contain highly sensitive or diplomatic information. This lack of clarity can lead to unauthorized exposure of sensitive data.

The specifics of how to handle highly sensitive data will require organizational policies to ensure compliance with legal and operational standards. The responsibility lies with data protection officers to define appropriate access control measures and handling protocols for sensitive information, which is beyond the scope of this feature proposal.
Answering this question requires organizational policies and decisions regarding the handling of highly sensitive data, which are beyond the scope of this feature proposal.

C2.challenge: The definition of 'full history of engagement' appears vague and unbounded. It is unclear if it encompasses all types of records or only selected interactions, which could lead to inconsistencies in what users expect to see.
C2.failure_scenario: A project manager expects to see emails and informal correspondence but the system only presents formal meeting notes, leading to incomplete preparation for the mission.
C2.resolution_test: List all specific types of records included in the 'full history of engagement'.

history.text: The definition of 'full history of engagement' appears vague and unbounded. It is unclear if it encompasses all types of records or only selected interactions, which could lead to inconsistencies in what users expect to see.

I revised the definition of 'full history of engagement' to explicitly include all types of engagement records, including informal communications, to ensure consistency in user expectations. This clarifies what users can expect to see in the engagement history.
Evidence: "D1: "full history of engagement" = A detailed log that includes all recorded interactions, meetings, emails, informal correspondence, and mission details related to a specified country."

C3.challenge: Assumptions regarding the completeness and accuracy of past engagement data are not robustly defined, leaving open the possibility of outdated or missing records, which can misinform project managers.
C3.failure_scenario: A project manager begins a mission based on incomplete historical data from the CRM, leading to unprepared confrontations with country representatives.
C3.resolution_test: What process will be implemented to ensure and verify the accuracy and completeness of engagement records before they are accessed?

The proposal does not detail the specific processes that will be implemented to verify the accuracy and completeness of engagement records, which could entail additional organizational decisions.

C4.challenge: The proposal does not specify what happens to access rights for project managers if they leave or change roles, which could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
C4.failure_scenario: A project manager leaves the organization but still has access to sensitive engagement records, leading to potential data breaches or unauthorized disclosures of sensitive information.
C4.resolution_test: What process is in place to manage access rights for project managers when they change roles or leave the organization?

history.text: The proposal does not specify what happens to access rights for project managers if they leave or change roles, which could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.

C5.resolution_test: What mechanisms are in place to ensure that project managers cannot filter engagement history to view sensitive records they do not have authorization for?
